chunks: It was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who goes out to Makkah without a guardian, and he said: "There is no harm; she may go out with trustworthy people."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman in question regarding travel
key_terms.قَوْمٍ: a group of people traveling with her
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the destination of the journey
key_terms.وَلِيٍّ: a guardian accompanying or overseeing her travel

ai.seo_question: Can a woman travel to Makkah for hajj without a guardian according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman traveling to Makkah without a guardian. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no harm in her doing so if she travels with trustworthy people, indicating the importance of safety and reliability in such travel.
